title: Collateral Protection Insurance — Reach Date for Faxed Proof Re-Reviews by Contract Status
content:
The reach date is the date from which the coverage-reach test of a faxed proof re-review under Collateral Protection Insurance measures the proof's expiration date. For a proof re-reviewed on a closed tracking record, the reach date is set by the borrower's contract under Retail Installment Contracts:

- **Contract paid off:** the reach date is the date of the first review, that is, the review date recorded on the proof's existing entry.
- **Contract not paid off but carrying a repossession date:** the reach date is the contract's repossession date (the date of the most recent recovery of the vehicle shown on the contract record).
- **Contract neither paid off nor carrying a repossession date:** the reach date is the re-review date.

## Points of judgement

| Contract record shows | Reach date |
|---|---|
| status paid off (whether or not a repossession date is also shown) | date of the first review |
| status other than paid off, with a repossession date | the repossession date |
| status other than paid off, no repossession date | the re-review date |

A paid-off status decides first: a contract that was repossessed, redeemed and paid off takes the date of the first review, not the repossession date.

**Hypothetical:** a proof first reviewed on a hypothetical day 0 shows an expiration date 40 days later, and is re-reviewed on day 60. On a paid-off contract the reach date is day 0, so the expiration date lies 40 days after it.
